summary: Iteration 3: 44/44 pytest backend tests pass (added 5 new tests for Key Activation feature — /api/stream/start-with-key + /api/stream/stop; refreshed 2 YouTube-status tests to match environment now that YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are populated). Frontend UI validated at mobile viewport 390x844: landing has no horizontal overflow, Features/Pricing nav links correctly hidden on mobile, Login/Get Started buttons visible; dashboard sidebar starts hidden (-translate-x-full) and hamburger toggle (top-left) slides it in (left: -256 -> 0) on click; LiveSlot page renders stream-key-card with key-video-select + stream-key-input + start-with-key-button for active-plan user, submitting a fake key returns success toast 'You are now live on YouTube!', UI swaps to stop-key-stream-button, and Stop reverts to Start. No-plan user sees the amber 'Activate a plan/slot to unlock streaming' notice with 'View Plans' CTA — inputs are correctly not rendered. All iteration 1+2 regressions still pass (auth, gatekeeping exact message, videos CRUD/rename/delete + storage decrement, streaming upload + incremental 2GB limit, Stripe webhook signature verification, idempotent plan activation, YouTube configured/authorize paths, checkout session/status/invalid plan, billings, support, dashboard stats, live-slot start/stop/settings).

minor.issue: No ffmpeg liveness check after spawn — with a fake/invalid stream key ffmpeg exits within 1-2s (expected here), but the live_streams document still reads is_live=true and current_video=... indefinitely until user manually stops. Consider a background reaper that polls os.kill(pid, 0) and flips is_live to false when the process dies.

Regular /api/live-slot/start (existing) and /api/stream/start-with-key both write to db.live_streams for the same user but with different fields (stream_key vs internal loop). If a user runs both paths back-to-back they update the same doc. This works today because start-with-key stops any existing ffmpeg first, but a defensive assertion (stream_method != 'youtube_oauth') might avoid confusing state.

Currently returns 404 'No active stream' if is_live is already false. That's spec-correct, but the frontend calls this via youtubeAPI.stopStream() from BOTH handleStopKeyStream and the OAuth flow; a 404 during the OAuth flow will surface an unnecessary error toast to the user. Consider making stop idempotent (return 200 with 'Already stopped' when no active record).

issues: The 'Live Slot Management' page heading is partially covered by the fixed hamburger button (top-left, z-50) at 390px viewport. Consider adding pl-16 or pt-16 to the main content wrapper on lg:hidden, or push the heading below the toggle.

The top-level 'Live Slot #1' card still exposes a green 'Start Streaming' button even though gating is enforced at the backend. It would be a better UX to visually disable this button (or hide it) when hasActivePlan is false, matching how the stream-key-card behaves — consistency with the amber notice pattern.

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Make POST /api/stream/stop idempotent (return 200 when nothing is live) so double-clicks / cross-flow calls don't emit spurious error toasts.
(Nice-to-have) Add a lightweight ffmpeg liveness reaper so live_streams.is_live reflects reality when ffmpeg dies on its own (fake key, network drop, YouTube revoke).
(UX) On mobile Live Slot page, offset the main content by the hamburger button's height so the page heading is not partially covered by the fixed top-left toggle.
(UX) Also gate the top-level 'Start Streaming' button on LiveSlot for no-plan users (currently only the stream-key-card branches on hasActivePlan).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to ~1094 lines — recommend splitting into APIRouter modules (auth, videos, payments, youtube, live_slot, stream_with_key, billings, support, dashboard). Iteration 2 flagged this too; still applies.
start-with-key correctly stops any existing ffmpeg PID before spawning a new one — prevents orphan processes.
start_ffmpeg_push failure is wrapped in try/except and surfaces as HTTP 500 with a generic 'Failed to start the video encoder' message — good.
CHUNK_SIZE bumped 1MB -> 8MB in upload_video is a safe optimization (still incremental storage-checked per chunk). The 2GB enforcement test with pre-seeded storage_used still passes.
on_event('startup'/'shutdown') is still deprecated in FastAPI — should migrate to lifespan handler (also flagged in iteration 2).

Frontend Navbar/Hero mobile-first tweaks are correct: 'hidden md:inline' on Features/Pricing, 'w-full sm:w-auto' on Hero CTAs, responsive text/padding — validated at 390x844 with no horizontal overflow.

DashboardLayout hamburger toggle button (line 42-49) has NO data-testid — added test worked around it via 'button:has(svg.lucide-menu)' but this should get a data-testid='mobile-sidebar-toggle' for maintainability.

youtube_service.start_ffmpeg_push writes ffmpeg logs to /tmp/ffmpeg_<key_prefix>.log — key prefix in filename is fine but the log itself contains the full rtmp URL including the key. Consider redacting the key in the ffmpeg command log/output when spawning.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (landing responsive, mobile sidebar toggle, key activation flow with-plan + no-plan)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 3 backend has two new endpoints: POST /api/stream/start-with-key (StreamKeyStart{video_id,stream_key,loop}) and POST /api/stream/stop. Both require an active plan (gatekeep returns 403 with the exact ⚠️ message). With a fake stream key ffmpeg exits ~1s later — this is EXPECTED, do NOT attempt to verify a real YouTube live. Backend YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are now populated in /app/backend/.env (contrast with iteration 2 which tested the 'not configured' paths); TestYouTubeNotConfigured has been updated accordingly — /api/youtube/status -> {configured:true, connected:false}, /api/youtube/oauth/authorize -> 200 with an authorization_url pointing at accounts.google.com. Frontend LiveSlot has a new data-testid='stream-key-card' with key-video-select / stream-key-input / start-with-key-button / stop-key-stream-button. Amber notice text 'Activate a plan/slot to unlock streaming' is shown when hasActivePlan is false. The dashboard hamburger toggle at lg:hidden has NO data-testid — add data-testid='mobile-sidebar-toggle' next iteration. pytest.ini enforces -n 2 --dist loadscope, so any new tests that mutate admin state should use a dedicated seeded fixture (see key_user fixture) to avoid parallel races with TestStorageEnforcement / TestVideos.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in iteration 3. Two pre-existing tests started failing because the environment gained real YOUTUBE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET between iteration 2 and 3; the tests (TestYouTubeNotConfigured) were updated to reflect the new configured state — this is a test-side environment sync, not an app regression. One new-test flake (test_upload_returns_ready_and_increments_storage seeing storage go 0 -> 18432 instead of 16384) was root-caused to a parallel-execution race with my new TestKeyActivation class which was uploading against the same admin session concurrently; fix was to give TestKeyActivation its own key_user fixture with an independently-seeded plan, isolating admin state from cross-class races. After that fix, all 44 tests pass repeatably.
